memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Take care of them until the fourteenth day of the month, when all the members
of the community of Israel must slaughter them at twilight." - Ex 12:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The lamb was chosen on the tenth day but killed on the fourteenth. Four days in
between. Why the wait?

Those four days were for inspection. The family lived with the lamb, watched it,
made sure it was truly without defect. And something else happened in those four
days that God surely intended: the family grew attached to it. A lamb in the
house for four days becomes familiar. Then it is killed. The cost of redemption
was meant to be felt, not merely observed.

There is a remarkable parallel in the Gospels. Jesus entered Jerusalem on what
we call Palm Sunday, and for the following days He was in the temple, publicly
examined by chief priests, Pharisees, Sadducees, and Herodians, all trying to
trap Him in His words. He was inspected in the open. Then, at Passover, He was
crucified. Pilate's verdict after examination was: "I find no basis for a charge
against him" (John 19:6).

The Lamb was tested in public view and found without fault. Nobody rushed this.
God let the world look closely first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you looked closely at Jesus, or only heard about Him second-hand?
2. Does the cost of your redemption still move you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from taking the cross casually. Let me look closely at Jesus and
never lose the wonder of what my salvation cost. Amen.
